document_check.note: The document is Hou Y, Liu F, Su G, Tu S, Lyu Z. 'Systematic review and meta-analysis of transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) for global cognition in mild cognitive impairment and Alzheimer's disease', Geriatric Nursing 59 (2024) 261-270. It reports the cited MMSE mean difference of 1.96 (95% CI 0.95 to 2.97, P = 0.0001) from 10 RCTs in 9 studies.

cited_result: tDCS versus control (sham in every trial) on MMSE: mean difference 1.96, 95% CI 0.95 to 2.97, P = 0.0001, random effects, I2 = 92%. The estimate comes from 10 RCTs in 9 studies (451 participants): four MCI-only trials (Zhang 2022, He 2021, Gomes 2019, Fileccia 2019) and six AD trials.
tool_reason: The cited result is a pooled mean difference from a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised trials, so ROBIS applies.

domains.rationale: The criteria (RCTs, clinically diagnosed MCI or AD, tDCS versus sham or non-tDCS, a global cognition outcome, English or Chinese) are appropriate. No protocol or registration is reported, so pre-specification cannot be verified. The outcome clause is open-ended ('such as ... etc'), and one exclusion criterion is vague.

signalling.question: 1.1 Did the review adhere to pre-defined objectives and eligibility criteria?
signalling.quote: Searched for a protocol, PROSPERO or other registration, or a statement that criteria were set a priori; none reported.

signalling.question: 1.2 Were the eligibility criteria appropriate for the review question?
signalling.quote: "Inclusion criteria: (1) study type: RCTs; (2) participants: patients with MCI or AD diagnosed clinically; (3) interventions: whether to use tDCS, or whether to use sham-tDCS or tDCS was the only intervention causing differences in results between the experimental and control group"

signalling.question: 1.3 Were eligibility criteria unambiguous?
signalling.quote: "(4) outcome indicators: inclusion of at least one indicator of global cognition, such as mini-mental state examination (MMSE), Montreal cognitive assessment test (MoCA), Milan overall Dementia assessment (MODA), P300 (including amplitude, latency and reaction time), etc"; "(3) studies with no comparable baseline information"

signalling.question: 1.4 Were all restrictions in eligibility criteria based on study characteristics appropriate?
signalling.quote: "(1) study type: RCTs"

signalling.question: 1.5 Were any restrictions in eligibility criteria based on sources of information appropriate?
signalling.quote: "were retrieved for relevant RCTs published in both English and Chinese languages from their respective inception through February 2023"

domains.domain: Domain 2: identification and selection of studies
domains.rationale: Ten English and Chinese databases were searched from inception, with two independent screeners and a third person to arbitrate. No supplementary methods are reported, and the full strategies are only in an appendix that is not in this text. These are minor shortfalls against an extensive search.

signalling.question: 2.1 Did the search include an appropriate range of databases/electronic sources for published and unpublished reports?
signalling.quote: "Ten databases, including PubMed, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, EBSCO, Embase, OVID, Chinese National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI), VIP Database for Chinese Technical Periodicals (VIP), Wanfang, SinoMed were retrieved"

signalling.question: 2.2 Were methods additional to database searching used to identify relevant reports?
signalling.quote: Searched for reference-list checking, trial-registry searching, citation tracking or contact with experts; none reported.

signalling.question: 2.3 Were the terms and structure of the search strategy likely to retrieve as many eligible studies as possible?
signalling.quote: "The combination of keywords and free words were used to build retrieval strategies"; "PubMed and Wanfang search strategies were provided as examples in the appendix."

signalling.question: 2.4 Were restrictions based on date, publication format, or language appropriate?
signalling.quote: "published in both English and Chinese languages from their respective inception through February 2023"

signalling.question: 2.5 Were efforts made to minimise error in selection of studies?
signalling.quote: "two researchers (Yufei Hou and Guiting Su) screened these studies by perusaling the title, abstract, and full text independently." [p2] (but an included trial is titled "a case-control study" [p9])

domains.domain: Domain 3: data collection and study appraisal
domains.rationale: Extraction and risk-of-bias assessment were done in duplicate with the Cochrane tool. However, results that eligible trials did report were not collected for synthesis: change-from-baseline data and data shown only in figures were set aside, and the document does not say that authors were contacted for these. Those set-aside trials are the ones described as showing no benefit.

signalling.question: 3.1 Were efforts made to minimise error in data collection?
signalling.quote: "Two researchers independently selected the literature, extracted the data, evaluated using the Cochrane Collaboration’s quality criteria, and then cross-checked."

signalling.question: 3.2 Were sufficient study characteristics available for both review authors and readers to be able to interpret the results?
signalling.quote: "The features of the included literatures were showed in Table 1." (Table 1 gives participants, diagnostic criteria, age, sample size, intervention, stimulation site, current intensity, frequency, duration and outcomes)

signalling.question: 3.3 Were all relevant study results collected for use in the synthesis?
signalling.quote: "three studies28,41,44 only reported data of the mean difference before and after the intervention, and two studies24,27 only showed the results in the chart without data, these studies could not be merged." [p3]; "one study42 showed the data of MMSE in chart." [p3]

signalling.question: 3.4 Was risk of bias (or methodological quality) formally assessed using appropriate criteria?
signalling.quote: "Two researchers (Shuzhen Tu and Zecai Lyu) used the Cochrane Intervention Systematic Review Manual 5.1.0 to independently evaluate the risk of bias"

signalling.question: 3.5 Were efforts made to minimise error in risk of bias assessment?
signalling.quote: "The difference of opinion was resolved through consultation with a third researcher (Fang Liu)."

domains.rationale: The MMSE pool leaves out trials that the review itself reports as showing no benefit (high-risk-of-bias exclusions, change-score-only and chart-only reports). The fixed or random model was chosen by an I2 threshold. MCI and AD trials are pooled with no diagnosis subgroup. I2 is 92%, and the sensitivity analysis drops three trials without a stated criterion. Publication bias was not assessed, and a trial its own title calls a case-control study is in the pool.

signalling.question: 4.1 Did the synthesis include all studies that it should?
signalling.quote: "Three studies26,36,43 had high risk of bias, three studies28,41,44 only reported data of the mean difference before and after the intervention, and two studies24,27 only showed the results in the chart without data, these studies could not be merged." [p3]; "showed that compared with placebo stimulation (sham-tDCS), tDCS could not promote the rehabilitation of the global cognition in AD." [p5]

signalling.question: 4.2 Were all pre-defined analyses reported or departures explained?
signalling.quote: "After excluding three studies,32,33,39 sensitivity analysis showed [MD = 1.76 95% CI (1.29, 2.23), P < 0.00001, I2 = 35%]" (no criterion for the exclusion and no protocol)

signalling.question: 4.3 Was the synthesis appropriate given the nature and similarity in the research questions, study designs and outcomes across included studies?
signalling.quote: "conversely, there is high heterogeneity between studies and the random-effects model was used, subsequently sensitivity or subgroup analysis was conducted." [p2]; "patients affected by mild cognitive impairment: a case-control study" [p9, reference 34, pooled in the MMSE analysis]

signalling.question: 4.4 Was between-study variation (heterogeneity) minimal or addressed in the synthesis?
signalling.quote: "We used a random-effects model (I2 = 92%)"; "The heterogeneity observed may be attributed to the difference stimulation frequency of tDCS and duration. And subgroup analysis on the basis of different durations." (duration subgroups of 2 to 3 studies; no MCI versus AD subgroup)

signalling.question: 4.5 Were the findings robust, e.g. as demonstrated through funnel plot or sensitivity analyses?
signalling.quote: Searched for funnel plot, Egger's test or any publication-bias assessment; none reported. The only sensitivity analysis is the unexplained exclusion of three studies: "After excluding three studies,32,33,39"

signalling.question: 4.6 Were biases in primary studies minimal or addressed in the synthesis?
signalling.quote: "Three studies26,36,43 had inconsistent data on outcome indicators before and after intervention and were judged as “-” for selective reporting. Others were judged as “?” or “+”."

domains.domain: Phase 3: risk of bias in the review
domains.rationale: The conclusions assert benefit and even prevention of conversion to AD, which none of the pooled outcomes measures. They do not address the exclusion of null trials, the very high heterogeneity, the pooling of MCI with AD, or the missing publication-bias assessment.

signalling.question: A. Did the interpretation of findings address all of the concerns identified in Domains 1 to 4?
signalling.quote: "The tDCS can ameliorate the global cognition of patients with MCI and AD, and it has a better rehabilitation effect than non-tDCS or sham-tDCS." [p1]; "which may be a safe nonpharmacological therapy to prevent MCI from developing into AD and to slow down the disease from progressing." [p8]

signalling.question: B. Was the relevance of identified studies to the review's research question appropriately considered?
signalling.quote: "Secondly, the diagnosis and outcome indicators of MCI and AD in the included literatures was not yet consistent, which may lead to bias in the results."

signalling.question: C. Did the reviewers avoid emphasising results on the basis of their statistical significance?
signalling.quote: "The meta-analysis found that tDCS increased MMSE, MoCA, MODA scores and reduced the P300 latency scores (all P < 0.05)."

applicability.rationale: The cited MMSE estimate pools four MCI-only trials with six AD trials and has no diagnosis subgroup, so it is not an MCI-specific estimate.

overall_rationale: Search and study selection are sound, but results were not collected from trials that reported change scores or figure-only data. The MMSE synthesis leaves out the trials described as null, uses a data-driven model choice, pools MCI with AD, carries I2 of 92% with a post hoc sensitivity analysis, and has no publication-bias assessment. The conclusions do not temper these concerns.
